root_cause.text: The bridge's neighbor suppression code used the compile-time macro `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` to check for IPv6 support, which does not account for IPv6 being disabled at runtime via the `ipv6.disable=1` kernel parameter, causing a NULL pointer dereference on the uninitialized `nd_tbl` when processing Neighbor Discovery packets.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "When booting with the 'ipv6.disable=1' parameter, the nd_tbl is never initialized... br_do_suppress_nd() will dereference ipv6_stub->nd_tbl which is NULL". The patch replaces `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` with `ipv6_mod_enabled()` in `br_device.c` and `br_input.c`, and the commit message explains: "Fix this by replacing IS_ENABLED(IPV6) call with ipv6_mod_enabled() in the callers. This is in essence disabling NS/NA suppression when IPv6 is disabled."

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace compile-time check with runtime check to ensure IPv6 neighbor suppression only activates when IPv6 module is actually enabled, preventing issues when IPv6 is built as a module but not loaded.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition in br_dev_xmit from compile-time check IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6) to runtime check ipv6_mod_enabled() for the IPv6 neighbor suppression case.
intent_record.how: The code now checks at runtime whether the IPv6 module is loaded and enabled, rather than assuming it is always available if compiled in, preventing potential issues when IPv6 is built as a module but not loaded.
